explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM judgments with human evaluation on the same 450 questions for answerability dimension, reporting Pearson correlation coefficients

prompts.notes: Paper mentions using 'direct prompts' and 'G-EVAL (Chain-of-Thought)' but does not provide the exact prompt text

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Improved from 0.181-0.559 in first round to 0.427-0.800 in second round

guidelines.notes: Scoring guidelines with 1-3 scale for each dimension provided in appendix, including specific scoring criteria and multiple annotation examples

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on 450 questions (30 passages) focusing only on answerability dimension due to budget constraints

quantitative_scores.notes: GPT-4 achieved the highest correlations but still below 0.4; methods using direct prompts and G-EVAL (Chain-of-Thought) compared
Performance compared with RQUGE, UniEval, and GPTScore-src (top three metrics on answerability)

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-based metrics (especially GPT-4) outperform other automatic evaluation methods but still show relatively low correlation (below 0.4) with human evaluation on answerability dimension, indicating room for improvement in LLM-judge alignment.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluation was conducted only on answerability dimension while human evaluation covered all 7 dimensions; validation focused on the shared criterion of answerability
